discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, trapping thousands of neutral atoms at a 'magic wavelength' so that the trapping light leaves the clock transition unperturbed. This combined the statistical power of many atoms with the isolation of a single trapped ion. Katori and Ye then turned the concept into instruments with fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and below, more than two orders of magnitude better than cesium standards. Ye's strontium clocks resolved the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample, and Katori's transportable clocks measured height differences at Tokyo Skytree. Together these results established relativistic geodesy. The clocks set new limits on variation of fundamental constants and on ultralight dark matter, and they motivate redefining the SI second. This is a new measurement paradigm, and it opens tests of gravity and quantum physics at the interface of general relativity and quantum mechanics.
